title: GitHub has alternatives, but no replacement
excerpt: Why forges like Codeberg, GitLab, and Forgejo can replace GitHub's code hosting—but not its shared social layer.
content_html:
Codeberg, a Git code hosting platform, recently took a decision to prohibit projects that mostly consist of generative-AI-written code which has prompted concern and extensive discussion elsewhere.

The decision does not surprise me, and I don’t mean that as a criticism. Codeberg has always presented itself as a mission-driven alternative to GitHub, not neutral infrastructure.1

What interests me is the disappointment in the response. Many people reacted as though one of the few plausible GitHub replacements had ruled them or their projects out. They wanted Codeberg to be a universal alternative, a better GitHub and the obvious place to go when leaving it.

To me, that exposes a big gap in the open-source space. There are plenty of places to host a Git repository, but remarkably few places to host an open-source community. GitHub gives projects a shared pool of identities, habits and paths to discovery. None of the alternatives has reproduced that at a similar scale.

I don’t think the answer has to be another centralized platform, or that every project should live in one place. But decentralization is not enough on its own. Whatever replaces GitHub still needs a shared social layer: identities contributors already have, conventions they understand and ways to discover projects across the network.

Why not self-hosting?#

Whenever dissatisfaction with GitHub comes up, someone inevitably says: “Git is decentralized. Just self-host a forge.”

I’ve self-hosted Gitea for years, so this is an argument I’m very familiar with. Self-hosting works well for personal projects, but I wouldn’t use it for something I wanted strangers to contribute to. On GitHub, most people already have an account and understand how issues and pull requests work. On my forge, even reporting a small bug means creating another account, learning how my forge works and what conventions I want you to follow. Unless someone really cared, they probably wouldn’t bother. I know I wouldn’t.

And contribution is only half of it. GitHub used to be genuinely good at discovery. I regularly found projects because someone I followed starred them, often in areas I would never have searched for myself. It felt like a social network built around people making things.

GitHub has since redesigned that feed, and I almost never visit it anymore. Defaults are powerful: once discovery stopped being part of the experience GitHub put in front of me, it largely disappeared from my workflow.

Why not GitHub?#

The basic experience of GitHub has been getting steadily worse. It is slow, things regularly fail to load and notifications are unreliable. GitHub itself recently described two major incidents as “not acceptable”.

Its pull request experience has been awful too. Large PRs are painfully slow to navigate and review. Stacked PRs2 have been common inside large software companies for well over a decade, but only just became a thing with GitHub and, even then, seems to be quite buggy.

What frustrates me about GitHub’s push towards AI is that the core forge feels neglected while Copilot appears everywhere. An agent writing more code doesn’t help when the interface for reviewing it is already struggling.

Ghostty exemplifies this frustration. In late April, Mitchell Hashimoto announced that Ghostty is leaving GitHub because frequent outages were preventing its maintainers from working reliably:

On the day I am writing this post, I’ve been unable to do any PR review for ~2 hours because there is a GitHub Actions outage. This is no longer a place for serious work if it just blocks you out for hours per day, every day.

Interestingly, he also makes the point that GitHub is more than hosting:

To the “Git is distributed!” crowd: the issue isn’t Git, it’s the infrastructure we rely on around it: issues, PRs, Actions, etc.

Hashimoto said Ghostty was in discussions with multiple commercial and FOSS providers and planned an incremental migration. The fact that such a prominent project had to shop around, rather than move to an obvious default, is exactly the gap I mean.

Why not the alternatives?#

It’s worth going through the alternatives and the problems I see with each:

GitLab is capable, but it feels incredibly corporate, even more so than GitHub.3 Nor have I found it as good as GitHub at helping people stumble across projects and developers.

SourceHut is focused and transparent and, like Codeberg, openly values-driven.4 Its email-oriented workflow, while battle-tested by projects like the Linux kernel, is unfamiliar to most GitHub users.

Forgejo’s federation project may eventually connect self-hosted instances into a shared network. It looks promising, but has been in development for quite some time, remains experimental5 and is not yet a practical answer to the social fragmentation of self-hosting.

Radicle is technologically interesting: repositories are replicated peer to peer, while issues and patches are stored alongside them. But it still feels too immature to replace GitHub for a public project. For example, its public web interface lets people browse repositories, but contributing requires them to install its CLI or desktop application. Someone encountering a bug should not have to install the forge’s software merely to report it.6

The project I’m most interested in is Tangled, based mostly on gut feel. I like its focus on the social experience around code. For example, its home page immediately shows me a bunch of cool projects, exactly like old GitHub used to do. But it is still in alpha, and it remains to be seen whether it can blossom into a true alternative.

Could a boring company fill the gap?#

One thing that stands out is that, apart from GitLab, every competitor is built around either decentralization or a social mission. That makes each of them fundamentally less “straightforward” than a for-profit company. It makes me wonder whether there is room for one.

Perhaps it could look more like bunny.net than a venture-backed startup: a deliberately boring company with no ambition to become the operating system for software development or to reorganize programming around whatever technology investors currently find exciting. It might simply concentrate on making open-source collaboration pleasant and reliable, charge developers and smaller organizations directly, and grow at whatever pace that revenue supports.

The open question is whether this could be a viable business. The difficult part is exactly what I keep saying is missing: shared identity, shared conventions and discovery only become valuable once a platform has reached scale. Better repository hosting alone would not solve that cold-start problem.7

I don’t know who, if anyone, will solve it. But a real replacement will have to treat the social layer as the product, not as something that appears automatically once enough repositories are hosted.

sentences.zh: 它看起来很有前途，但已经开发了相当长一段时间，仍处于实验阶段5，并且还不是解决自托管社会碎片化问题的实际答案。

blocks.html_en: Radicle is technologically interesting: repositories are replicated peer to peer, while issues and patches are stored alongside them. But it still feels too immature to replace GitHub for a public project. For example, its public web interface lets people browse repositories, but contributing requires them to install its CLI or desktop application. Someone encountering a bug should not have to install the forge’s software merely to report it.6

sentences.en: Radicle is technologically interesting: repositories are replicated peer to peer, while issues and patches are stored alongside them.
sentences.zh: Radicle 在技术上很有趣：存储库是点对点复制的，而问题和补丁则与它们一起存储。

sentences.en: But it still feels too immature to replace GitHub for a public project.
sentences.zh: 但以公共项目取代 GitHub 仍然感觉太不成熟。

sentences.en: For example, its public web interface lets people browse repositories, but contributing requires them to install its CLI or desktop application.
sentences.zh: 例如，它的公共 Web 界面允许人们浏览存储库，但贡献需要他们安装其 CLI 或桌面应用程序。

sentences.en: Someone encountering a bug should not have to install the forge’s software merely to report it.6
sentences.zh: 遇到错误的人不应该仅仅为了报告它而安装伪造的软件。6

blocks.html_en: The project I’m most interested in is Tangled, based mostly on gut feel. I like its focus on the social experience around code. For example, its home page immediately shows me a bunch of cool projects, exactly like old GitHub used to do. But it is still in alpha, and it remains to be seen whether it can blossom into a true alternative.

sentences.en: The project I’m most interested in is Tangled, based mostly on gut feel.
sentences.zh: 我最感兴趣的项目是《魔发奇缘》，主要基于直觉。

sentences.en: I like its focus on the social experience around code.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢它对围绕代码的社交体验的关注。

sentences.en: For example, its home page immediately shows me a bunch of cool projects, exactly like old GitHub used to do.
sentences.zh: 例如，它的主页立即向我展示了一堆很酷的项目，就像旧的 GitHub 过去所做的那样。

sentences.en: But it is still in alpha, and it remains to be seen whether it can blossom into a true alternative.
sentences.zh: 但它仍处于 alpha 阶段，是否能发展成为真正的替代品还有待观察。

blocks.html_en: Could a boring company fill the gap?#

sentences.en: Could a boring company fill the gap?#
sentences.zh: 无聊的公司能填补这个空白吗？#

blocks.html_en: One thing that stands out is that, apart from GitLab, every competitor is built around either decentralization or a social mission. That makes each of them fundamentally less “straightforward” than a for-profit company. It makes me wonder whether there is room for one.

sentences.en: One thing that stands out is that, apart from GitLab, every competitor is built around either decentralization or a social mission.
sentences.zh: 值得注意的一点是，除了 GitLab 之外，每个竞争对手都是围绕去中心化或社会使命构建的。

sentences.en: That makes each of them fundamentally less “straightforward” than a for-profit company.
sentences.zh: 这使得它们从根本上来说不如营利性公司“直接”。

sentences.en: It makes me wonder whether there is room for one.
sentences.zh: 这让我想知道是否有空间容纳一个。

blocks.html_en: Perhaps it could look more like bunny.net than a venture-backed startup: a deliberately boring company with no ambition to become the operating system for software development or to reorganize programming around whatever technology investors currently find exciting. It might simply concentrate on making open-source collaboration pleasant and reliable, charge developers and smaller organizations directly, and grow at whatever pace that revenue supports.

sentences.en: Perhaps it could look more like bunny.net than a venture-backed startup: a deliberately boring company with no ambition to become the operating system for software development or to reorganize programming around whatever technology investors currently find exciting.
sentences.zh: 也许它看起来更像bunny.net，而不是一家由风险投资支持的初创公司：一家故意无聊的公司，没有雄心成为软件开发的操作系统，也没有围绕目前投资者认为令人兴奋的任何技术重新组织编程。

sentences.en: It might simply concentrate on making open-source collaboration pleasant and reliable, charge developers and smaller organizations directly, and grow at whatever pace that revenue supports.
sentences.zh: 它可能只是专注于使开源协作变得愉快和可靠，直接向开发人员和小型组织收费，并以收入支持的任何速度增长。

blocks.html_en: The open question is whether this could be a viable business. The difficult part is exactly what I keep saying is missing: shared identity, shared conventions and discovery only become valuable once a platform has reached scale. Better repository hosting alone would not solve that cold-start problem.7

sentences.en: The open question is whether this could be a viable business.
sentences.zh: 悬而未决的问题是这是否是一项可行的业务。

sentences.en: The difficult part is exactly what I keep saying is missing: shared identity, shared conventions and discovery only become valuable once a platform has reached scale.
sentences.zh: 困难的部分正是我一直说的缺失的部分：共享身份、共享约定和发现只有在平台达到规模后才变得有价值。

sentences.en: Better repository hosting alone would not solve that cold-start problem.7
sentences.zh: 仅靠更好的存储库托管并不能解决冷启动问题。7

blocks.html_en: I don’t know who, if anyone, will solve it. But a real replacement will have to treat the social layer as the product, not as something that appears automatically once enough repositories are hosted.

sentences.en: I don’t know who, if anyone, will solve it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道谁（如果有人）能解决这个问题。

sentences.en: But a real replacement will have to treat the social layer as the product, not as something that appears automatically once enough repositories are hosted.
sentences.zh: 但真正的替代者必须将社交层视为产品，而不是一旦托管了足够多的存储库就会自动出现的东西。

content_html_zh:
Git 代码托管平台 Codeberg 最近决定禁止主要由人工智能生成代码组成的项目，这引起了其他地方的关注和广泛讨论。

这个决定并不让我感到惊讶，我的意思并不是批评。 Codeberg 始终将自己定位为 GitHub 的任务驱动替代品，而不是中立的基础设施。1

我感兴趣的是回应中的失望。 许多人的反应就好像 GitHub 上少数几个看似合理的替代品之一已经排除了他们或他们的项目。 他们希望 Codeberg 成为一个通用的替代方案、一个更好的 GitHub，以及离开它后显而易见的去处。

对我来说，这暴露了开源领域的巨大差距。 有很多地方可以托管 Git 存储库，但可以托管开源社区的地方却很少。 GitHub 为项目提供了一个共享的身份、习惯和发现路径的池。 没有一个替代方案能够以类似的规模复制这一点。

我认为答案不一定是另一个中心化平台，或者每个项目都应该存在于一个地方。 但权力下放本身还不够。 无论取代 GitHub 的是什么，仍然需要一个共享的社交层：贡献者已经拥有的身份、他们理解的约定以及通过网络发现项目的方法。

为什么不自行托管？#

每当出现对 GitHub 的不满时，总会有人说：“Git 是去中心化的。 只需自行建立一个熔炉即可。”

我已经自行托管 Gitea 多年，所以这是我非常熟悉的一个论点。 自托管非常适合个人项目，但我不会将其用于我希望陌生人做出贡献的事情。 在 GitHub 上，大多数人已经拥有一个帐户并了解问题和拉取请求的工作原理。 在我的熔炉中，即使报告一个小错误也意味着创建另一个帐户，了解我的熔炉如何工作以及我希望您遵循哪些约定。 除非有人真正关心，否则他们可能不会打扰。 我知道我不会。

而贡献只是其中的一半。 GitHub 曾经非常擅长发现。 我经常找到一些项目，因为我关注的人给它们加了星标，通常是在我自己永远不会搜索的领域。 感觉就像一个围绕人们创造事物而建立的社交网络。

此后 GitHub 重新设计了该 feed，我几乎不再访问它了。 默认设置非常强大：一旦发现不再成为 GitHub 呈现在我面前的体验的一部分，它就基本上从我的工作流程中消失了。

为什么不是 GitHub？#

GitHub 的基本体验一直在不断恶化。 它很慢，经常无法加载内容，并且通知不可靠。 GitHub 本身最近将两起重大事件描述为“不可接受”。

它的拉取请求体验也很糟糕。 大型 PR 的导航和审核速度极其缓慢。 十多年来，堆叠式 PRs2 在大型软件公司中已经很常见，但直到 GitHub 才成为一种现象，即使如此，似乎也存在很多问题。

GitHub 对人工智能的推动让我感到沮丧的是，核心锻造者感觉被忽视了，而 Copilot 却无处不在。 当审查界面已经很困难时，代理编写更多代码并没有帮助。

幽灵就是这种挫败感的例证。 4 月下旬，Mitchell Hashimoto 宣布 Ghostty 将离开 GitHub，因为频繁的中断导致维护人员无法可靠地工作：

在我写这篇文章的那天，我已经有约 2 个小时无法进行任何 PR 审查了，因为 GitHub Actions 发生了故障。 如果这里只是让你每天花几个小时，那么它就不再是一个严肃工作的地方了。

有趣的是，他还指出 GitHub 不仅仅是托管：

到“Git 已分发！” 人群：问题不是 Git，而是我们所依赖的基础设施：问题、PR、操作等。

Hashimoto 表示，Ghostty 正在与多家商业和 FOSS 提供商进行讨论，并计划进行增量迁移。 事实上，这样一个突出的项目必须货比三家，而不是转向明显的默认，这正是我所说的差距。

为什么不选择替代方案？#

值得仔细研究一下替代方案以及我在每个方案中看到的问题：

GitLab 很有能力，但它给人的感觉令人难以置信，甚至比 GitHub 还要强。3 在帮助人们偶然发现项目和开发人员方面，我也没有发现它像 GitHub 那样好。

SourceHut 专注且透明，并且像 Codeberg 一样，公开地以价值观为驱动。4 其面向电子邮件的工作流程虽然经过了 Linux 内核等项目的实际测试，但对大多数 GitHub 用户来说并不熟悉。

Forgejo 的联合项目最终可能会将自托管实例连接到共享网络中。 它看起来很有前途，但已经开发了相当长一段时间，仍处于实验阶段5，并且还不是解决自托管社会碎片化问题的实际答案。

Radicle 在技术上很有趣：存储库是点对点复制的，而问题和补丁则与它们一起存储。 但以公共项目取代 GitHub 仍然感觉太不成熟。 例如，它的公共 Web 界面允许人们浏览存储库，但贡献需要他们安装其 CLI 或桌面应用程序。 遇到错误的人不应该仅仅为了报告它而安装伪造的软件。6

我最感兴趣的项目是《魔发奇缘》，主要基于直觉。 我喜欢它对围绕代码的社交体验的关注。 例如，它的主页立即向我展示了一堆很酷的项目，就像旧的 GitHub 过去所做的那样。 但它仍处于 alpha 阶段，是否能发展成为真正的替代品还有待观察。

无聊的公司能填补这个空白吗？#

值得注意的一点是，除了 GitLab 之外，每个竞争对手都是围绕去中心化或社会使命构建的。 这使得它们从根本上来说不如营利性公司“直接”。 这让我想知道是否有空间容纳一个。

也许它看起来更像bunny.net，而不是一家由风险投资支持的初创公司：一家故意无聊的公司，没有雄心成为软件开发的操作系统，也没有围绕目前投资者认为令人兴奋的任何技术重新组织编程。 它可能只是专注于使开源协作变得愉快和可靠，直接向开发人员和小型组织收费，并以收入支持的任何速度增长。

悬而未决的问题是这是否是一项可行的业务。 困难的部分正是我一直说的缺失的部分：共享身份、共享约定和发现只有在平台达到规模后才变得有价值。 仅靠更好的存储库托管并不能解决冷启动问题。7

我不知道谁（如果有人）能解决这个问题。 但真正的替代者必须将社交层视为产品，而不是一旦托管了足够多的存储库就会自动出现的东西。
